note: Seven register trees inside the archaeological park, within about 2 km of each other: a walk (paid entry to the park counts as public). The register gives no ages; online figures run from 300 to over 1,000 years for the olives, so any age needs a named source and stays as vague as it gives it. Several sit near the Kolymbetra garden (FAI, its own ticket); check which side of that gate each trunk stands. A second r/sicily reader (2026-10-23, no name kept) adds that at least one olive there is 'in the 300+ range' (hearsay, no source). Pins are register coordinates, default approximate. Under own-supply pause: nothing ships until a photo is approved and supply reopens; a Commons sweep of the park is the next cheap step.

blocked.name: The olive of Borgo Giallonardo
blocked.place: Borgo Giallonardo, Realmonte (Agrigento), a country hotel
blocked.source: reader tip on r/sicily, 2026-10-23 (no name kept): 'an absolutely huge olive tree on the ground of Borgo Giallonardo', 'by far the largest olive tree I have ever seen'; staff told them several hundred years, nobody knows exactly
blocked.reason: access: it stands in a hotel's grounds, so a visitor may need the reception's permission (hard rule 10). Open again if a source shows non-guests can walk in, or a reader sends a photo and says how they got there.
